name: Archit Nuwood Industries Ltd
tagline: Small-cap MDF/HDF and pre-laminated board manufacturer riding a real furniture/interiors import-substitution tailwind, with genuinely strong FY24 headline returns (ROCE ~40-60%, ROE ~57-60%) - but this pass confirms the FY24 profit was accompanied by deeply negative operating cash flow (-Rs 10 Cr) and a quadrupling of debt, and FY25 PAT actually fell even as revenue grew 75%, raising real profit-quality questions the original write-up had flagged as unresolved.
business_overview: Founded in 2017 (Tohana, Haryana), Archit Nuwood Industries manufactures MDF and HDF boards and pre-laminated boards for the furniture/interiors value chain, benefiting from domestic import-substitution dynamics (anti-dumping duties on Chinese/other MDF imports) and India's organised-furniture growth. Listed via SME IPO (BSE SME, listed Sep 6, 2024; fresh issue of 62.4 lakh shares raising Rs 168.48 Cr). Promoters Prem Chand, Vinod Kumar Singla and Vineet Kumar held 93.92% pre-IPO, diluted to 69.15% post-IPO. The company does not own the registered trademark 'ARCHIT NUWOOD' or 'NUWUD' (a disclosed IPO risk factor), and the promoters have an outstanding personal legal proceeding relating to a GST penalty. Seeded via X triage (untrusted, @Disciplined_Inv, very-high conviction, 2026-09-13).
fundamentals_table: ROCE ~40.4% (original pass) to ~60.6% (screener 'current', basis unclear); ROE ~57.3-60.4%
Rs 40 Cr -> Rs 134 Cr -> Rs 152 Cr -> Rs 184 Cr -> Rs 322.58 Cr (FY25, +75% YoY)
Rs 3 Cr -> Rs 4 Cr -> Rs 21 Cr -> Rs 37 Cr -> Rs 28.13 Cr (FY25, DOWN ~24% despite +75% revenue growth)
Revenue Rs 236.50 Cr, PAT Rs 38.69 Cr (already exceeds full FY25 PAT; margin recovered to ~16.4% from FY25's ~8.7%)
Borrowings jumped Rs 6 Cr (FY23) -> Rs 35 Cr (FY24); operating cash flow was -Rs 10 Cr despite Rs 37 Cr PAT
Debtor days 49 -> 97 (also cited elsewhere as 71 -> 97.2); working-capital days -10 -> 96 (also cited as 10.5 -> 96.4)
fundamentals_narrative: The original write-up correctly flagged FY24's headline ROCE/ROE (~40-60%) alongside a sharply worsening working-capital trend as an unresolved caution. This deep-dive pass confirms the underlying concern is real and more serious than day-count metrics alone suggested: FY24 operating cash flow was -Rs 10 Cr despite Rs 37 Cr of reported PAT, funded by borrowings that jumped from Rs 6 Cr to Rs 35 Cr in one year - profit was not converting to cash, and debt was rising to plug the gap, consistent with the debtor-days blowout (49->97) and working-capital-days blowout (-10->96) in the same year. FY25 then saw revenue nearly double (+75% to Rs 322.58 Cr) but PAT actually FELL to Rs 28.13 Cr (down ~24% from FY24) - a margin collapse (~20% to ~8.7%) consistent with either the FY24 profit-quality problem catching up (bad-debt provisioning, aggressive prior recognition unwinding) or genuine competitive/cost pressure on the larger revenue base. The most recent data point is more encouraging: 9M FY26 PAT of Rs 38.69 Cr (on Rs 236.50 Cr revenue) already exceeds full FY25 PAT, with margin recovering to ~16.4% - a genuine improvement, though fresh FY25/FY26 cash-flow and working-capital-day figures could not be sourced this pass to confirm whether the underlying cash-conversion problem has actually resolved or merely paused. The India MDF/HDF import-substitution tailwind (anti-dumping protection, organised-furniture growth) remains real and structural, independent of this company-specific execution question.

verdict_headline: Small-cap MDF/HDF board maker with a real import-substitution tailwind and a genuine 9M FY26 margin recovery - but this pass confirms the FY24 return ratios came with deeply negative operating cash flow and quadrupled debt, and FY25 PAT actually fell despite 75% revenue growth. four_box softened to 3.0 (valuation downgraded on profit-quality grounds); conviction further capped at Low-Medium pending fresh cash-flow confirmation.
verdict_reasoning: Deep-dive pass 1 confirms (rather than merely flags) the working-capital caution the original pass identified: FY24's strong headline PAT (Rs 37 Cr) was accompanied by -Rs 10 Cr operating cash flow and debt quadrupling (Rs 6 Cr -> Rs 35 Cr) - a real profit-quality issue, not just deteriorating day-count ratios.

New finding: FY25 PAT fell ~24% despite 75% revenue growth - directly consistent with the FY24 cash-conversion problem unwinding, though not proven as the specific mechanism. 9M FY26 shows a genuine recovery (PAT already exceeding full FY25), but fresh cash-flow/working-capital data to confirm the underlying issue is resolved could not be sourced this pass.

four_box revised to 3.0 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak - unchanged, young company with no strong brand/scale moat; valuation downgraded weak - the ~17.3x P/E is being computed off profit numbers with a documented cash-quality caveat). Score still permits the return-magnitude label per the small/mid-cap rule; thesis_fit retained at 10x-in-2-3-years rather than overridden to neither, since (unlike other names reviewed this pass) there is no confirmed ongoing deterioration - the trajectory is genuinely ambiguous (FY24 bad, FY25 worse, 9M FY26 better).

No red-flag-tier trigger found (no auditor resignation, no promoter pledge, no company-level SEBI/fraud action - only a promoters' personal GST-penalty proceeding and a trademark-ownership gap, both disclosed IPO risk factors). Conviction downgraded Medium -> Low-Medium given the confirmed profit-quality issue and continued zero community corroboration.
